# Prefill attention core, generated by stream-dse

`softmax(q @ k_t) @ v` for every head, generated by stream-dse as one design whose
outermost loop runs over the heads.
It covers the part of prefill attention that `iron/applications/llama_3.2_1b` still runs
on the host; the projections around it stay on IRON's own GEMM.

```python
op = MHAPrefillStream(seq_len=256, d_head=64, heads=2, context=ctx)  # flash=True to block the key
op.compile()
run = op.get_callable()
run.get_buffer("q").torch_view()[:] = q.flatten()      # already scaled by 1/sqrt(d_head)
run.get_buffer("k_t").torch_view()[:] = k_t.flatten()  # already transposed
run.get_buffer("v").torch_view()[:] = v.flatten()
run()
context = run.get_buffer("output").to_torch().reshape((heads, seq_len, d_head))
```

## What the caller does, and why

**`q` arrives pre-scaled.** Folding `1/sqrt(d_head)` into the query is exact and saves an
elementwise pass over the whole `seq x seq` score matrix.

**`k_t` arrives transposed.** An ONNX `Transpose` is a layout node that cuts the fusion
group, and the generated design has no operand transform to undo one. The host already
transposes K in the llama prefill path, so this costs nothing new.

## One group or three

`k=1` puts all three layers in one design. The softmax reads its row linearly while the
GEMM either side of it writes and reads a MAC-tiled layout, so the score and the
probability matrix are **staged on a memory tile** on the way between them: a plain copy
from the producing core into the tile, then a transformed transfer out of it that re-lays
the tile out row major. That transform needs four dimensions and a core DMA takes three,
so the hop through the tile is what makes the fusion possible. Neither matrix touches a
shim or DDR. A head's whole key and value stay resident on the cores that read them,
32 KB of a 64 KB core at `seq_len = 256`, which bounds the query tile to 16 positions.
That leaves no room to prefetch the next head's key beside it, so stream holds one copy
and prices the refill each head waits for.

`k=3` puts each layer in its own design; the three are fused into one ELF, but each keeps
its own `aie.device` and is configured in turn, so every intermediate goes out to DDR and
back once per layer.

Where each layer runs is stream-dse's to derive; the operator declares only each layer's
kernel arguments and the fused groups.

## Causal masking

`causal=True` masks every key at a later position than its query, which is what prefill
computes. The whole key row is resident on the core that reduces it, so a query attends a
prefix of that row: the softmax kernel writes `-inf` over the suffix past the query's own
position, then normalizes the row as before. The iteration space does not change, so the
mask costs the writes it makes and saves no work. The kernel is handed the tile's global
first row, which the stream-dse binding builds from the core's spatial index and the loop
over the query.

## Blocking the key

`flash=True` runs the softmax **online**: the key is cut into blocks of 64, and each block
is normalized against a running row maximum and sum instead of against the whole row. The
context then accumulates over the key exactly the way a GEMM's output accumulates over its
contraction, so nothing in the workload reduces nonlinearly and the key is an ordinary
blockable dimension. The kernels are `linalg/mha.cc`'s online-softmax entry points, which
mask in global positions, so flash is always causal and skips every block past the
diagonal.

The query block is 32 or 64 rows against the 64-wide key block, and stream-dse chooses
between them: 32 spreads a short sequence over more cores, 64 halves the calls on a long
one. The running scale, `[m_{i-1} | m_i | l_i | exp2(m_{i-1} - m_i)]`, stays on the
softmax core, which reads and writes it across key blocks. A copy of it crosses to the
context core every key block through a two-deep object fifo in the memory the two cores
share, which costs no DMA channel and lets the two cores run a key block apart.

## Limits

- **The query is the only dimension a core may split**: the head dimension is the score
  GEMM's contraction and the backend has no cross-core accumulation, and the key is the
  softmax's reduction.
- **Without flash the sequence is bounded by what stays resident.** The fused score core
  holds the whole key beside its own tiles, which `_check_shapes` caps at 320 positions.
- **Flash takes `d_head = 64` and a `seq_len` that is a multiple of 64 and at most 8192.**
  `mha.cc` reuses the score GEMM's compiled block for the value matmul, and past 8192
  the query transfer needs one more iteration than a shim buffer descriptor holds.

## Measuring

`python -m iron.common.stream.model_check sweep OUT --operators mha` times the design
stream chooses and every candidate on the NPU; `report OUT` compares them with stream's
estimates.
